tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the catalog of real products stocked by the suppliers on file. Accepts Persian or English. Returns normalized facets (mounting, indoor/outdoor, IP, colour temperature) plus what the query matched on. Colour temperature is returned but is NOT filterable: a fixture is usually sold in several, a

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Every field on file for one product, by the id search_products returns ('brand/product-slug'), including provenance: whether the fact came from the supplier's own website or from a page of their PDF catalog, and when it was read.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: The 20 canonical categories with Persian and English names, product counts, and which suppliers are in each. Small enough to fetch once and reason over the whole market; flags categories that only one supplier covers.

tools.name: list_brands
tools.description: Every supplier on file with what they cover, how complete their data is, and when it was last read. No contact details — see the server instructions.

tools.name: get_brand
tools.description: One supplier in full: what they make, the product families they run, and — the field worth the call — doesNotDo, a statement of what they genuinely do NOT make, computed from absence in their product list rather than inferred from their marketing.

tools.name: compare_brands
tools.description: Which suppliers cover a category, with counts, share, and per-facet data coverage. Coverage describes what each supplier's SOURCE stated, never product quality, and a one-supplier category says so rather than pretending to be a comparison.

tools.name: classify_lighting_term
tools.description: Map any Persian or English lighting phrase onto the canonical taxonomy — «داون‌لایت توکار», 'trimless plaster frame', 'high bay'. Backed by 522 learned type→category pairs plus rules measured at 95% agreement. Returns null for a phrase that names no category rather than guessing.

tools.name: start_consultation
tools.description: Turn a described need into a link the person opens themselves, where an adviser builds a brief and matches it against suppliers' real stock. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "search_products" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "search_products" appears informational but accepts parameters (environment) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: q, category, brand, environment, mounting, ip_min, price_tier, has_image, limit, offset

findings.title: Hidden characters in tool description
findings.detail: Description of "classify_lighting_term" contains 1 invisible/zero-width or bidi character(s). Legitimate descriptions have no reason to hide text the model still reads.
